description: Chapter-shape archetypes for progression fiction. These are structural conventions of the genre — the stock shapes a serial chapter can take — not the plot of any particular book. Each says how it opens, where it turns, how it closes, what it is for, what it costs, and how it fails. The framework generator composes one of these with the arc, the beat, and the live state.
how_to_use: Pick the shape that serves the beat the tempo asks for. A 'pressure' beat is not a shape; 'the squeeze' and 'the demonstration' are two very different ways to deliver it.

shapes.name: The Demonstration
shapes.for: Establishing competence in front of people invested in the protagonist not having it.
shapes.open: Mid-task, already behind. The reader meets the skill before the biography.
shapes.turn: The task turns out to be a test, or the audience turns out to matter.
shapes.close: Success that costs standing, or success nobody is willing to credit.
shapes.failure_mode: The competence is narrated instead of dramatised; the reader is told he is good rather than shown a problem only he could solve.

shapes.name: The Threshold Test
shapes.for: A formal evaluation that sorts people, run by an institution with its own interests.
shapes.open: The rules are stated, and one of them is unfair in a way nobody comments on.
shapes.turn: The protagonist finds the gap between the rule as written and the rule as enforced.
shapes.close: He passes by the gap. Someone notices the gap, not the pass.
shapes.failure_mode: The test is a formality the reader knows he will pass. If there is no version of the scene where he fails, there is no scene.

shapes.name: The Squeeze
shapes.for: Two obligations that cannot both be met, on the same deadline.
shapes.open: The second obligation arrives while the first is already late.
shapes.turn: He finds a way to serve both, badly, and the cost of the compromise becomes visible.
shapes.close: He chooses. The one he dropped is a person, and they know.
shapes.failure_mode: One option is obviously correct. Both must be defensible or it is not a squeeze.

shapes.name: The Quiet Acquisition
shapes.for: The protagonist gains something substantial without anyone noticing — the core loop of a progression novel, and the chapter type most likely to be boring.
shapes.open: An ordinary errand in a place where something is ending.
shapes.turn: He recognises the value nobody else can see, and takes it.
shapes.close: A second person almost saw. Almost.
shapes.costs: residue, or the person who paid
shapes.failure_mode: It becomes a shopping list. The gain must be observed by the reader as theft, gift, or scavenging — it must have a moral temperature.

shapes.name: The Workshop
shapes.for: A profession chapter: craft under pressure, where the craft is the conflict.
shapes.open: Materials, constraints, and a deadline that belongs to someone else.
shapes.turn: Something fails — and failure is more generous than success.
shapes.close: The piece is finished, wrong, or finished wrongly. A professional judges it.
shapes.failure_mode: Process porn with no stake. Someone must be able to lose something by the end of the making.

shapes.name: The Hunt
shapes.for: Going somewhere dangerous for a resource, with a clock.
shapes.open: The party, the terms, and the thing nobody has said aloud about the ground.
shapes.turn: The ground is worse than briefed, or a companion's agenda surfaces.
shapes.close: They get it, or they get most of it, and carry something back that was not on the list.
shapes.failure_mode: Combat as spectacle. The fight must resolve a question the chapter asked before it started.

shapes.name: The Offer
shapes.for: Patronage with terms. The genre's real inflection point, more than any fight.
shapes.open: A room he was not invited into until now, and the reason he is there is flattering.
shapes.turn: The terms are read properly, and they are worse and better than they sounded.
shapes.close: Accepted, refused, or deferred — all three are decisions, and all three cost.
shapes.failure_mode: The offer is obviously a trap. A good offer is genuinely good, which is what makes taking it a character choice instead of a plot event.

shapes.name: The Witness
shapes.for: Someone sees something they should not have, and the chapter is about what they do with it.
shapes.open: POV may or may not be the one seeing. Consider giving this chapter to the observer.
shapes.turn: The observer decides what it is worth.
shapes.close: Silence, sale, or leverage — and the protagonist does not learn which for chapters.
shapes.failure_mode: The observer is a plot device. Give them their own agenda that has nothing to do with the protagonist.

shapes.name: The Breakthrough
shapes.for: Realm advance, under pressure, at a price. Never a scheduled milestone.
shapes.open: The pressure first. The advance must be the only way through, not a reward for grinding.
shapes.turn: It works, and something breaks that was load-bearing.
shapes.close: He is stronger and worse off. Someone felt it happen.
shapes.costs: body, anonymity — always something that does not come back
shapes.failure_mode: The numbers were met three chapters ago and the reader is waiting. Break through when the story demands it, not when the sheet allows it.

shapes.name: The Reckoning
shapes.for: Something the protagonist did earlier comes back with a face on it.
shapes.open: An ordinary day interrupted by a name from the record.
shapes.turn: The reader realises which chapter this is paying off before the protagonist does.
shapes.close: The debt is collected, deferred at interest, or refused — never dissolved.
shapes.costs: whatever he saved earlier, with interest
shapes.failure_mode: The callback is to something the reader has forgotten. Check `novel.py lookback` and re-seed it two chapters earlier if needed.

shapes.name: The Rest That Isn't
shapes.for: A low-tension chapter that lowers tension and raises dread.
shapes.open: Genuine relief. Food, repair, company, sleep. Let it be real.
shapes.turn: One detail is wrong, and only the reader catches it.
shapes.close: Warmth, and the wrong detail still sitting there.
shapes.costs: nothing yet — that is the point
shapes.failure_mode: Nothing happens. A rest chapter still needs a want, even a small one: a conversation someone is trying to have and failing.

shapes.name: The Reveal To One Person
shapes.for: The protagonist tells one person a true thing, and the novel changes shape.
shapes.open: A reason they are alone that neither engineered.
shapes.turn: He tells a smaller truth to test the ground.
shapes.close: The other person's reaction is not the one he priced. Record it; it is load-bearing forever.
shapes.costs: anonymity, and the ability to un-tell it
shapes.failure_mode: Used too early. This chapter is only worth what the concealment cost to maintain.

shapes.name: The Humiliation
shapes.for: A public loss that sets the terms of everything after it.
shapes.turn: The loss is not from weakness but from a rule he did not know was in play.
shapes.close: He does not vow revenge. He goes and finds out what the rule was.
shapes.failure_mode: Humiliation as motivation fuel. The scene must cost him something concrete — a place, a patron, a friend — not just feelings.

shapes.name: Two Rooms
shapes.for: Cutting between two scenes whose meanings change each other, where neither is interesting alone.
shapes.turn: Room B reveals what Room A is actually about.
shapes.close: End in the room the reader is more afraid of.
shapes.failure_mode: Two subplots stapled together. The cut must do work no single-room version could.
